name: Ulicia

facts.text: Altan Garran (about 336,000/315,500 in Cothrom Gorge) is a walled outlander town of faction Outland Residents: Outland garda (49-53), conaitheoir (48-51), bardach (48-53) and asarlai (49-57), merchants (Egomas the smith, Halwyn, Paili, Noirin the enchanter, Forsa, Gearoidin the healer, Alastair and Luiseach Erea) and garran treants; its named are Fedail, Elnara Erea, Ulicia, Aodhnait, Ansol, Fachtna, Zinsya and Declan, all set aggressive (200) in the world data.
Irish garda 'guard', cónaitheoir 'resident', asarlaí 'sorcerer'; 'Altan Garran' read as altán 'ravine' + garrán 'grove' (to verify).

Ulicia: level 52, model 743 (the model of the town's asarlai and bardach), faction Outland Residents, aggressive, at about 336,500/318,000 on the south side of Altan Garran beside Luiseach Erea's stall.
Living Server lore: Ulicia as the asarlai who keeps the south watch against Tachtwort.

story:
Altan Garran is the only town in Cothrom Gorge, and it is not a Sylvan town. Its people are outlanders: Sylvan and half-Sylvan families who left Domnann over the generations, for quarrels, for debts, for love, for the wardens' law, and went down into the gorge where the wardens do not walk, and built a walled grove of their own on the gorge's eastern ledges. They keep their own garda on the walls, their own bards and sorcerers, their own markets, and their own opinion of strangers, which is low. The Domnann wardens call them the outlanders and trade with them when they must. Hibernians who walk up to the gate unannounced are generally met at it.

The outlanders' sorcerers are the asarlai, and the town has a handful of them, trained in no grove the Domnann wardens would recognise. Ulicia is the eldest. She keeps the south side of Altan Garran, the side Tachtwort has been eating for a generation, and she keeps it alone, because the families who lived there have all moved north across the square. Her house is the last one lit on the south side. Luiseach Erea's instrument stall stands beside it, and the town says that is because the Ereas will not let the south side be empty while one of them is still selling harps.

Every night Ulicia walks the south wall with the garda and burns the tendrils that have come through the stones during the day, and every morning there are more. She has done it so long that her hands are scarred to the wrist with the wort's sap. The outlanders' bards make songs about her that she will not listen to. The garda say she is the reason the south side still has a wall at all, and that the worst thing that could happen to the town would be for her to die on a night when the tendrils are thick.

She does not like Hibernians any better than Elnara does. She has a different reason. The young swords who come to the gate cut Tachtwort down, she says, and take its remains to Fedail and feel they have done something, and in the morning it is standing under the wall again and she is still on the south side with her burning-sticks. Noirin the enchanter says that if anyone in the town will be glad on the day Marfoirwort dies, it will be Ulicia, and that she will not say so.
legend: Ulicia (52) is an Outland Residents sorceress-type named on the south side of Altan Garran, near Luiseach Erea's stall and close to Tachtwort's wall. The town is set aggressive in the world data, so she and the nearby garda can attack Hibernians. No script; at 52 with the asarlai model expect a caster-style fight, so interrupt and burn. Do not fight her with Tachtwort (76) right outside the wall. A 50s group with a puller; pull from the south edge away from the square. The outlanders' bards sing about her; the garda say the south wall stands because of her.

loremasterTopic.text: The eldest asarlai of Altan Garran in [Cothrom Gorge], who keeps the south side alone against [Tachtwort], burning its tendrils out of the wall every night.

bookPage: Noirin the enchanter of Altan Garran: Ulicia's is the last lit house on the south side. Everyone else moved across the square when Tachtwort's tendrils came up through the floors. She walks the south wall with the garda every night and burns the tendrils out of the stones, and every morning there are more, and her hands are scarred to the wrist with the sap. She dislikes Hibernians for cutting Tachtwort and feeling they have done something. If anyone in the town is glad the day Marfoirwort dies, it will be Ulicia. She will not say so, not to me and not to anyone.
